text: Harsimrat Kahlon (1982 – October 4, 2009) was an Indian-Canadian serial killer who murdered three of her newborn infants between 2005 and 2009 in Calgary. After her death from complications of childbirth on October 4, 2009, her common-law husband Harnek Mahal discovered the infants' bodies stuffed in a suitcase and a box, reporting the findings to police, who later determined the children had been murdered by their mother. Kahlon was born in Chandigarh, India in 1982, to Sikh parents. In 1999, she emigrated to Canada, settling with her aunt and uncle in Martindale. She worked as an assistant and receptionist at a law firm, where colleagues described her as a hard worker who appeared happy. Her live-in boyfriend, Harnek Mahal, was a long-haul trucker who worked away from home, and the couple were described as quiet and reserved. They initially lived in a basement suite in Falconridge before moving to Taradale in 2006. On October 4, 2009, after returning home from work, Mahal found Kahlon lying face-down in her bedroom, motionless; he called the police, who ruled her death as non-suspicious due to childbirth complications. The next day, Mahal reported finding a suspicious suitcase in a garbage bag with blood and other fluids dripping from it. A medical examiner opened the bag and found a newborn infant inside. A more thorough search, conducted by Mahal's sister just hours later, uncovered another box containing two additional corpses and a placenta. Mahal stated he knew Kahlon had been pregnant in the early 2000s and that they had agreed she would have an abortion, but he was unaware of the other two pregnancies. Forensic psychologist Dr. J. Thomas Dalby concluded Kahlon likely suffered from a personality disorder or depression, resulting in an unstable personality and self-loathing. In her secret diary, Kahlon expressed no guilt about the children's deaths but showed some attachment to them, as she kept the bodies on her property after their deaths. The first child, Reet Kahlon, was a girl born in 2005 at the Peter Lougheed Centre to an unknown father and was found wearing a hospital ID bracelet. The other two infants, unnamed, were born alive at home in the summer of 2009 while Mahal was away. Bloodied towels, sheets, clothing, cloths, and a garden hose were used as crude instruments during the killings, and Kahlon hid the bodies in her bedroom, spraying air freshener to mask the odor of decaying flesh. Questions about why Kahlon killed the children and why she kept the bodies remain unanswered, and the case has been officially closed by authorities.
